About border components

This collection has 38 border components for React, focused on outlines, edges, and animated frames. You'll find gradient borders, glowing outlines, and animated variants like a beam that travels around the edge of a card or button. Some add moving light effects; others are static accents for panels and inputs. If you're after a border beam or other animated borders to frame a component, these give you the effect as reusable markup.

Use a static gradient outline for a quiet accent, and an animated beam when you want an element to catch the eye. Wrap it around a card, button, or input as a container. Copy the TSX, install via the shadcn CLI with the registry URL, or pull it through the Magic MCP in your editor. They're Tailwind-based and use Motion for the moving-edge animation.

About features components

This collection holds 199 feature components for laying out what a product does. You get bento grids, icon-and-text rows, alternating image splits, tabbed showcases, and card layouts that scale from three items to a dozen. Styles run from clean enterprise sections to playful animated blocks. It is the section that sits below the hero and carries the bulk of a page's message, so variety in rhythm and density matters here.

Choose a bento grid when features differ in weight and a uniform card row when they are peers. Each piece is React plus Tailwind CSS, ready for a Next.js page without setup. Grab the TSX from the source view, install through the shadcn CLI with the registry URL, or pull it into your editor via the Magic MCP. Pair it with a matching hero and pricing block for a coherent page.

About button components

This collection gathers 764 React button components, from plain shadcn-style buttons to spotlight and floating action variants. You get primary, secondary, ghost, outline, and destructive states, plus icon buttons, loading buttons, and animated hover treatments. Many follow shadcn/ui conventions, so variants and sizes map to the props you already expect. Whether you need a simple form submit or a glowing call to action, there is a version here to start from.

Reach for a basic shadcn button when you want a neutral base you can theme; pick a spotlight or animated one when the click target needs to pull focus. Every button ships as full TSX with a live preview, so you can copy the code straight in, run npx shadcn@latest add with the registry URL, or pull it through the Magic MCP from Cursor or Claude Code. They are Tailwind-based and drop into any Next.js or React app.
